text: Hello again!
Last time, we learned something clever.
When adding gets stuck, a friend can rescue us.
Do you remember the trick?
We take away the friend, and then we add five.
Today the beads get stuck a different way.
This time, we are taking away.
The rule is still the same as last time.
Always look at the lower beads first.
If there are enough, just take them away.
Let us try nine take away two.
Make nine on your abacus.
Now take two lower beads away.
That was easy.
Nine take away two is seven.
No friend needed there at all.
Now let us try five take away one.
Make five on your abacus.
Look carefully at the lower beads.
How many lower beads do you have?
None at all.
The upper bead is holding all of the five.
So how can we take one away?
There is nothing down here to take.
Look at that, we are stuck.
Do not worry, we know what to do.
One's friend is four.
Last time, the friend helped us add.
This time, the friend helps us take away.
Here is the trick.
First, we add the friend to the lower beads.
Then, we take away five.
Remember, lower beads move first.
So add four lower beads now.
The rod shows nine.
Now take away five.
Push the upper bead up.
The rod shows four.
Five take away one is four.
We had nothing to take, and we still did it.
Let us try six take away two.
Make six on your abacus.
Look at the lower beads.
There is only one, and we need two.
So we call a friend.
Two's friend is three.
Add three lower beads first.
The rod shows nine.
Now take away five.
Push the upper bead up.
The rod shows four.
Six take away two is four.
You are doing so well with these tricky ones.
If you are enjoying this, please like the video and subscribe.
Now, let us try one more together.
Let us try seven take away four.
Make seven on your abacus.
Look at the lower beads.
There are two, and we need four.
Four's friend is one.
Add one lower bead first.
The rod shows eight.
Now take away five.
Push the upper bead up.
The rod shows three.
Seven take away four is three.
Did you see the pattern?
It is the same trick as last time, just the other way round.
Last time, we took away the friend, and then added five.
This time, we add the friend, and then take away five.
Every time, we did the same two things.
Add the friend first.
Then take away five.
The friend changes.
The five never does.
Now it is your turn, all on your own.
Make six on your abacus.
Then take away three.
Think about it.
What is three's friend?
Add that friend to the lower beads first.
Then take away five.
What number is showing now?
Six take away three is three.
Did you get it right?
Well done, you used the trick all by yourself.
Now you know the small friends for taking away too.
Try them on your own abacus at home.
Search for abacus kids on the Apple App Store or Google Play.
Download it free.
Next time, we will mix everything together in one big game.
See you next time!
